text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Mubarak discusses with Arab leaders the recommendations of the foreign ministers meeting on how to face Israel's hardline policy. Recommendations were reached by total consensus; Foreign Minister Moussa says peace is a strategic option with its fate in Israel's hands.

- The government is working towards raising the standard of living and not raising the prices of services in 1996 and 1997. Prime Minister Ganzouri says Egypt will also try to increase urban and agricultural lands to 40 million acres from the current 10 million within the next two decades.
- Arab foreign ministers end meetings in Cairo, decide on three-stage political plan to push forward the peace process. Ministers suggested long, medium and short-term policies.
- Ahli is the champion of Arab football teams, beating Morocco's Raga'a 3-1 in a fine match.
- Egypt inaugurates cotton bourse in Alexandria.
- Mubarak receives report on results of Arab League meeting; contacts Arab leaders for talks on ministerial recommendations.
- Egypt sends 40 tonnes of aid to Sudanese flood victims.
- Electronic alarms to secure archeological sites and Egyptian Museum.
- State announces cotton prices, inaugurates Mena Bassal cotton bourse.
- Mubarak met Kuwaiti, Syrian and Lebanese foreign ministers. Egypt does not accept any violation of Iraq's independence and sovereignty.
- Netanyahu, behave! (front page headline of editorial)
- Moussa says Mubarak contacting Arab leaders for talks on recommendations to revive peace, discounts summit meeting to be held for such talks.
- Defence Minister Tantawi says Egyptian forces constantly training to combat weapons of mass destruction.
